options.text: The value is 2/3 because -1/(x-2) from 3 to 5 = -1/3 + 1 = 2/3.

questions.explanation: Antiderivative -1/(x-2); from 3 to 5 = -1/3 + 1 = 2/3. The value is 2/3. The negative sign is essential.

questions.subject: CALCULUS_I
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a definite integral of distinct linear factors
questions.stem: An architect integrates 1/((x-1)(x+2)) from 2 to 3 and claims the value is 1/3 ln(2/5).

options.text: The claim is correct because partial fractions give 1/3 ln|(x-1)/(x+2)|.
The claim is correct because the denominator is degree 2.
The claim is wrong because distinct factors need quadratic numerators.

The claim is wrong because the coefficient is 1/3? Let's solve: 1/((x-1)(x+2)) = A/(x-1)+B/(x+2). 1 = A(x+2)+B(x-1). x=1: A=1/3. x=-2: B=-1/3. Integral = (1/3)ln|x-1| - (1/3)ln|x+2| = (1/3)ln|(x-1)/(x+2)|. From 2 to 3: (1/3)(ln(2/5)-ln(1/4)) = (1/3)ln(8/5). So claim 1/3 ln(2/5) is wrong (missing evaluation at lower). Value = (1/3)ln(8/5).

questions.explanation: The value is (1/3)ln(8/5), not (1/3)ln(2/5). The claim ignores the lower limit. Partial fractions coefficient is 1/3.

questions.subject: CALCULUS_I
questions.learningObjective: Explain divergence of an improper integral of 1/x^p for p<=1
questions.stem: An architect's brief asks why integral from 1 to infinity of 1/x^2 converges but 1/x diverges.

answer.exemplar: For 1/x^2, p=2>1, the antiderivative -1/x tends to 0 at infinity, giving a finite value 1. For 1/x, p=1, the antiderivative ln x grows without bound, so it diverges. The p-integral test threshold is p>1 for convergence.

questions.explanation: p=2>1 converges to 1; p=1 diverges because ln x→∞. The threshold p>1 determines convergence.

questions.subject: CALCULUS_I
questions.learningObjective: Set up integration by parts for x^2 e^x
questions.stem: An architect's brief needs the antiderivative of x^2 e^x and must explain the parts setup.

answer.exemplar: Choose u=x^2, dv=e^x dx, so du=2x dx and v=e^x. Parts gives x^2 e^x - ∫ 2x e^x dx. The remaining integral needs another parts application. Differentiating the polynomial reduces its degree, which is the goal.

questions.explanation: Parts with u=x^2 gives x^2 e^x - ∫2x e^x dx. The remaining integral needs another parts. Differentiating the polynomial reduces degree.
